extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, totaling 50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices). Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report, and each volume is annotated with 18 abnormalities. The dataset was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital and is divided into training and internal validation sets.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, and collaborators from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, NIH, Imperial College London, University Hospital Zurich, and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
extraction.publisher: Istanbul Medipol University / University of Zurich
extraction.rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE is a novel dataset consisting of chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. The cohort was divided into training (20,000 patients) and validation (1,304 patients) groups. Every reconstructed volume from the hospital database was incorporated to support comprehensive evaluation of various abnormalities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. External validation sets were sourced from the public RAD-ChestCT dataset and the UPMC dataset (MedSyn paper).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing personal information of patients and medical professionals using regular expressions to identify and remove date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. Reports were translated from Turkish to English using Google Translate API, with translations reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students. CT volume metadata was anonymized to remove identifying information.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: CT volumes were excluded if they involved contrast material or body parts other than chest. Each CT volume's orientation was standardized by examining metadata. Each volume was resized to uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in z-axis. CT volumes were center-cropped or padded to a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. Volumes were converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from metadata, with HU values clipped to range of -1000 to 1000, then normalized to a range of -1 to 1 during training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1,000 reports were manually annotated by merging findings and impression sections, creating a multi-label dataset identifying 18 abnormalities per report. Similar conditions were grouped (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; various lung opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules). The annotated reports were divided 80/20 for training/validation. The RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m pretrained language model was finetuned on this dataset and then used to classify the remaining 24,692 reports for 18 distinct abnormalities. For CT-CHAT, over 2.7 million question-answer pairs were generated using Llama 3.1 7B/8B LLM.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned RadBERT model's precision, recall, and F1 scores were evaluated showing robust classification across abnormalities. Classification thresholds were determined by identifying the left-upper point on the ROC curve using 10% of each validation set.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 18 abnormality labels per CT volume/report; 1,000 reports manually annotated for finetuning the automated labeler
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected translations and removed residual personal information. Three board-certified radiologists (two from Zurich, one from Istanbul) evaluated report generation outputs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned language model for automatic label extraction); Llama 3.1 7B/8B (for generating VQA question-answer pairs); Google Translate API (for Turkish to English translation); TotalSegmentator (for anatomical/nodule segmentation labels)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The CT-RATE dataset is publicly accessible via Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE. Future work plans to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes patient age (18-102 years) and sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male). All chest CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports were anonymized before computational analysis, with personal information of patients and medical professionals removed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models address critical challenges in 3D medical imaging and lay the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care. AI has potential to efficiently identify pathologies, reduce workload on radiologists, and potentially save lives where immediate radiological expertise is not available. However, experts emphasized that substantial progress is still needed for clinical deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Biases inherent to the single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may limit the generalizability of models to other populations. The dataset captures substantial heterogeneity in CT scanners (Philips 61.5%, Siemens 30.1%, PNMS 8.4%), acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Biases inherent to single-institution dataset may limit generalizability. CT-CLIP depends on specific terminology used in reports and the choice of prompts during zero-shot detection. Evaluation of CT-CHAT faces limitations due to lack of pretrained 3D medical multimodal AI assistants for benchmarking. Current models are limited to chest CT volumes. The generated reports' quality remains insufficient for clinical use, underscoring the need for further improvements and clinical validation before deployment in routine radiology workflows.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Used for developing CT-CLIP (contrastive language-image pretraining framework), CT-CHAT (vision-language AI assistant for 3D chest CT volumes), multi-abnormality detection, volume-to-volume retrieval, report-to-volume retrieval, radiology report generation, and visual question answering.
